scope: Representation/geometric/function/decomposition literature screening only; no implementation or training performed by this research pass.
shared_contract: Use only Local256, already-read Base/Gap forward512 and availability. Sanitize inactive values with where before projection; no backward-half reads. Every utterance starts fresh. No Memory/query/task-head/loss change, support examples, extra history, missing-modality reconstruction, or additional dependencies. First valid utterance and padding return original path; output corrections for inactive slots remain exactly zero. Source algorithm transfer is not source whole-model reproduction or evidence of task benefit.

cards.title: An evidential classifier based on Dempster-Shafer theory and deep learning
cards.source_domain: Image/signal/semantic-relation classification; not MSA or conversational emotion recognition.
cards.source_verification: Read original paper and raw author code. The author implementation incorrectly gives Omega three product terms in DS3_Dempster; the paper-based formula below explicitly fixes this discrepancy. DS1_activate also applies a sample-max rescale that is omitted in the proposed formula-based port.
cards.mechanism: Prototype distance -> discounted support -> singleton/ignorance mass -> complete normalized conjunctive combination. For prototype j, s_j=alpha_j exp(-gamma_j ||x-p_j||^2), m_j(c)=s_j u_jc, m_j(Omega)=1-s_j. Given a,b, n_c=a_c b_c+a_c b_Omega+a_Omega b_c; n_Omega=a_Omega b_Omega; Z=sum_c n_c+n_Omega; m=n/Z; conflict=1-Z. Omega is computed separately, never by applying singleton formula to the whole vector.
cards.transfer: For each active role, retain role/head identity in its vector projection and compute several latent prototype masses. Fuse only these already-read role masses. Expose fused singleton masses, Omega and conflict to a linear residual bridge. Use a modest latent frame, not true emotion-class probabilities. Bound alpha below one so vacuous support keeps Z positive, compute products in a stable scale, and preserve an explicit high-conflict diagnostic.
cards.difference: NetVLAD sums center residuals; VB capsules infer Gaussian assignments; RAT-SPN marginalizes a decomposable density. DST explicitly represents set-valued ignorance and incompatible mass through conjunctive fusion. Prototype distances alone do not qualify; all combination stages must remain.
cards.difference_from_retained9: Not DPP subset diversity or a Boolean truth-table circuit: combination operates on belief mass intersections and an ignorance state, with conflict normalization.
cards.resolved_previous_pending: The prior source-code discrepancy is resolved at design level by selecting an explicitly paper-derived implementation and documenting the incorrect author master. Acceptance still requires testing that implementation, not trusting the repository label.
cards.mask: Inactive roles contribute vacuous mass (all singleton masses zero, Omega one), exactly the identity of normalized combination. Exclude inactive prototype evaluations before distances. Empty history bypasses the branch.
cards.risk: Correlated Base/Gap are not independent evidence sources; latent masses are not calibrated uncertainty. Near-total conflict can amplify errors. Retaining nonzero Omega reduces numerical danger but does not validate source assumptions.
verification_required: Omega formula against exhaustive set intersection
Finite task gradients and adversarial inactive NaN invariance

cards.title: B-cos Networks: Alignment is All We Need for Interpretability
cards.source_verification: Original PDF pages 3-5 read directly via pypdf; Eqs. 8-14 give full-network composition and Sec. 3.2.3 gives MaxOut. Raw official forward code inspected. This closes previous unavailable-method-text pending.
cards.mechanism: Each layer uses row-normalized w and T_B(x;w)=(w_hat dot x)|cos(w_hat,x)|^(B-1). Two candidate weight rows per neuron use source MaxOut. Compose every internal layer with this transform, without ordinary ReLU/BN. For B=2 use a|a|/sqrt(||x||^2+epsilon). The effective network matrix is the product of input-dependent layer matrices.
cards.transfer: Concatenate masked fixed role/head projections and availability, apply a complete bias-free B-cos-MaxOut network, then the normal linear zero residual bridge. One cosine gate around an ordinary MLP is specifically disallowed. Source 1x1 convolution is algebraically a vector transform; no spatial head grid is introduced.
cards.difference: Directional normalized transforms replace all internal affine/nonlinear layers; no content branch is merely rescaled by a scalar reliability head. Layerwise dynamic linearity is a mechanism of the entire branch.
cards.difference_from_retained9: KAN composes edge functions; Lattice interpolates tables; Sandwich couples weights for a Lipschitz bound. B-cos instead ties nonlinear magnitude to directional alignment across all layers.
cards.resolved_previous_pending: Complete method text and full author forward inspected; retain the full composed B-cos architecture instead of the previously feared isolated cosine gate.
cards.mask: Sanitize all inactive coordinates before forming the fixed vector; availability is an explicit observed coordinate. Never include inactive values in the cosine norm. No history means zero correction.
cards.risk: Original alignment/interpretability results use BCE on the full classifier and special image encoding. Those claims do not transfer to a small branch under unchanged OSRAM loss; only the transform is retained. Large B or small input norms can cause weak gradients.
verification_required: B=1 reduces to normalized MaxOut linear map
Nonzero gradients to all B-cos weights

cards.title: Multiplicative Filter Networks
cards.source_domain: Continuous image, shape and differential-equation function representation.
cards.source_verification: Primary paper search cache exposes recursion and Section 3.2; author publication page links this exact paper/repository, official conference slides provide equations. Direct PDF requests currently hit OpenReview anti-bot; raw author implementation is fully read. This limitation is disclosed rather than calling the full PDF downloaded.
cards.mechanism: g_l(x)=sin(Omega_l x+phi_l) exp(-gamma_l ||x-mu_l||^2/2); z_0=g_0(x); z_l=g_l(x) elementwise*(W_l z_(l-1)+b_l). Every layer filters the same original x; only the recurrent hidden mixing is linear. A final linear map reads the multi-filter product expansion.
cards.transfer: Project sanitized fixed-role evidence to a compact coordinate vector, then use the entire Gabor MFN. Latent x is a feature-domain coordinate, not physical time/pixels. Positive gamma via softplus is an explicit numerical adaptation; source gamma is only initialized positive. Use bounded/scaled input to avoid high-dimensional envelope underflow, with fixed settings before experiments.
cards.difference: Withdrawn methods factor a finite bilinear/polynomial interaction of embeddings. MFN repeatedly reinjects nonlinear localized sinusoidal filters of the complete input and composes their product expansion. A single Gabor feature map followed by an MLP, or separate FourierNet and GaborNet counting, is not allowed.
cards.difference_from_retained9: KAN has nested learned univariate edge functions; MFN's nonlinear filters always see original input, with an input-dependent multiplicative recursion. It is not a KAN activation variant.
cards.mask: Mask each role before projection; input availability preserves absence identity. Exclude unavailable coordinates from any direct distance if role-wise filters are used. Skip no-history rows.
cards.risk: Periodic/localized latent response may overfit and has no established relation to emotion structure. Multiplicative attenuation and unconstrained source gamma are numerical risks. AGPL source is an inspection reference; implement equations independently rather than copying code.

cards.title: Towards Certifying L-infinity Robustness using Neural Networks with L-inf-dist Neurons
cards.source_verification: Original PMLR paper identity and mechanism verified; raw official distance kernels and wrapper fully read. Source exposes mean_normalize=False, so no batch-statistics replacement is needed for that configuration.
cards.mechanism: A neuron is h_j^(l+1)=||h^l-w_j^l||_infinity+b_j^l; compose distance layers throughout the branch. Parameters are centers in incoming representation space, not dot-product weights. Exact max absolute-coordinate difference, not an RBF gate plus MLP.
cards.transfer: Use sanitized fixed-slot projection as h0, then a complete distance network and a linear readout bridge. Set mean_normalize=False; use exact infinity norm in train/eval for a fixed function without source p-annealing or robust hinge objectives. This intentionally trades the original optimization recipe for protocol compatibility.
cards.difference: NetVLAD pools residual vectors with soft assignments; here repeated learned-center maximum-distance maps define the network. There is no token clustering or normalization-only wrapper.
cards.difference_from_retained9: Sandwich preserves dot-product networks using Cayley-coupled constraints; distance layers are nonlinear in input-center differences and need no spectral/Cayley constraint. Shared robustness motivation is allowed but algorithms differ.
cards.mask: Sanitize inactive inputs before projection; when applying a distance directly in unprojected fixed coordinates, omit inactive coordinates from max rather than measuring their zero-to-center distance. No history bypasses.
cards.risk: Exact max gives sparse subgradients and source training used a smoother continuation. The branch may be 1-Lipschitz relative to its input but arbitrary projection, bridge and Flat invalidate whole-model certification. Do not claim certified missingness robustness.

cards.title: Sum of Squares Circuits
cards.source_domain: Tractable density estimation and probabilistic circuit expressiveness.
cards.source_verification: Original paper plus author-project link verified; raw SOS code inspected. The code explicitly squares each signed/complex circuit before integrating it, not the already-integrated amplitude.
cards.mechanism: Structured-decomposable amplitude circuits c_j have unrestricted signed weights; density score s(x)=sum_j |c_j(x)|^2, normalized by the exact partition integral. Signed cross terms allow cancellation before squaring. Preserve multiple compatible squares rather than squaring one ordinary positive SPN output.
cards.transfer: Build a small continuous Gaussian-basis circuit over role/head coordinate projections with a fixed partition tree, signed sum layers and decomposable products. Read multiple normalized log-score features through the task bridge. Implement pair-circuit contraction for exact marginalization/partition; no generative/NLL objective and no cirkit dependency are introduced. This is a discriminatively trained density-feature module, not a recovered input model.
cards.difference: RAT-SPN uses nonnegative normalized mixtures without destructive cross terms. SOS combines signed amplitudes and contracts their squares, so marginalization requires cross-basis integrals. It is neither a new random SPN partition nor a compressed affine tensor-train layer.
cards.difference_from_retained9: Logic-gate networks mix Boolean truth tables; this is a continuous amplitude circuit with exact integration. Same circuit family does not mean the same core algorithm.
cards.mask: For an inactive scalar replace paired leaf product phi_a(x)phi_b(x) by its analytic overlap integral. Do NOT set each amplitude leaf to one and square later: integral(c^2) is not square(integral(c)). Apply per-mask marginal contraction; empty history bypasses.
cards.risk: Cancellation creates tiny scores; signed arithmetic, pair-state growth and partition normalization need careful FP64 checks. Small scalar projections may bottleneck evidence. Source probabilistic guarantees apply only to the declared learned coordinate density, not original modalities or calibrated emotions.

cards.title: Theoretical Linear Convergence of Unfolded ISTA and Its Practical Weights and Thresholds
cards.source_domain: Sparse signal recovery and compressed sensing.
cards.source_verification: Original NeurIPS method, exact author repository and forward recurrence read; source paper explicitly distinguishes per-sample support from its image experiment's cross-batch support selection. Only the former is admissible here.
cards.mechanism: Keep measurement y anchored throughout inference: v_k=z_k+W_k(y-Az_k); z_(k+1)=eta_(theta_k,S_k)(v_k), where large-magnitude support S_k is exempt from soft thresholding, and all other coordinates use signed shrinkage. Weight coupling is expressed through the residual y-Az rather than independent dense recurrent weights.
cards.transfer: Each complete masked fixed-slot vector projects to y; a fixed seeded normalized overcomplete dictionary A and learned W_k/thresholds define sparse code pursuit from z0=0. Use the resulting code as features, never decode a missing modality. A fixed source-style support schedule and per-sample ranking are chosen before any performance screen. Joint task training does not claim exact sparse recovery.
cards.difference: Closest is CRATE, not merely RPCA. CRATE alternates subspace attention with a one-step nonnegative dictionary sparsification of current tokens. CPSS repeatedly pursues one original y, tracks explicit coding residual and exempts a growing estimated support from signed shrinkage. Hamburger factorizes a per-sample nonnegative matrix; RPCA separates low-rank and corrupt coordinates. No separate counts for LISTA/ALISTA/depth variants.
cards.difference_from_retained9: Not ODE/DEQ equilibrium or KAN; finite sparse pursuit has explicit residual consistency and support selection. Broad optimization/sparsity motivation remains shared.
cards.mask: Build y only from sanitized active slots plus availability; ranking is per utterance, never across batch. For a masked measurement-coordinate variant use m*(y-Az) and a correspondingly masked encoder. First-history bypass.
cards.risk: High mechanism proximity to CRATE must be reviewed, not hidden. If implementation drops input anchoring or support exemption it becomes an old-ISTA variant and must be rejected. Dictionary mismatch and unconstrained learned W invalidate source convergence theorem.
verification_required: Task gradients to all learned W and thresholds

cards.title: Building Deep Networks on Grassmann Manifolds
cards.source_domain: General visual recognition including HDM05 activity and PaSC face verification; source also evaluates AFEW facial emotion videos, explicitly disclosed. It is not MSA/MERC.
cards.source_verification: Original Eqs. 2-7 read. Eq. 6 and surrounding text explicitly allow A-ProjPooling across projection matrices, whereas inspected MATLAB vl_mypooling realizes the within-matrix spatial variant. Use the paper's across-matrix version; do not claim the MATLAB demo implements this exact pooling selection.
cards.mechanism: For several subspace branches Q_j, use full-rank FRMap W_jQ_j -> thin QR -> P_j=Q_jQ_j^T. A-ProjPooling averages projectors across branches; OrthMap takes the leading q eigenspace of the average; a further FRMap/ReOrth and final projector generate the vector representation. Across-branch pooling/rank reduction is essential.
cards.transfer: Each fixed role's entire head-ordered vector is linearly lifted to an ambient-dimension by q basis matrix and made full-rank via a fixed orthogonal anchor. Role identity is in separate lifts/branches; columns are latent basis coordinates, not heads. Pool projected branch subspaces and retain final role-aware output bridge. Use q smaller than pooled span dimension so this cannot collapse to merely composing linear FRMaps.
cards.difference: SPDNet learns spectral functions of covariance magnitude; GrNet identifies a q-dimensional subspace modulo basis rotation and performs projector averaging followed by rank-q eigenspace selection. It discards basis choice, not the head labels used to construct each matrix.
cards.difference_from_retained9: Hyperbolic exp/log geometry encodes negative curvature; this is compact Grassmann quotient geometry. No orthogonal invariance of arbitrary OSRAM channel triples is presumed.
cards.resolved_previous_pending: Earlier head-identity concern is addressed by fixed ordered-vector lifts before introducing basis columns. AFEW involvement is disclosed rather than presented as wholly unrelated to emotion recognition.
cards.mask: Only active-role projectors enter the average and denominator. Zero/padding matrices never enter QR. Full-rank anchor and q constraints are checked; no-history bypasses. All matrix states are utterance-local.
cards.risk: Basis quotient may discard useful amplitude information; anchors and eigengap regularization are explicit migration choices. Degenerate eigenspaces require projector-based stable gradients. Simply stacking FRMap+QR without across-branch pooling is not an acceptable complete port.
verification_required: Right basis rotation Q->QR leaves projector unchanged
Permuting raw head coordinates still changes encoded input generally

cards.title: Differentiable Compositional Kernel Learning for Gaussian Processes
cards.source_domain: Gaussian process kernel composition, regression and extrapolation.
cards.source_verification: Primary paper Sec. 3.1 and author main repository README inspected. The core lives in the author-linked GPflow-Slim dependency; raw neural_kernel_network.py and neural_kernel_network_wrapper.py read, including softplus-positive weights and fixed product grouping.
cards.mechanism: Evaluate primitive PSD kernels on each active token pair; alternate k'_a=sum_b softplus(w_ab) k_b + positive constant kernel with fixed groups k''_g=product_(a in group_g) k'_a. Retain at least two full sum/product composition modules and multiple final kernel channels. Every intermediate unit remains a kernel by PSD closure.
cards.transfer: Use role/head-aware projected vectors; evaluate RBF, rational-quadratic and linear primitive kernels between current readout tokens, not between training examples. The full composed pair-kernel tensor is read with fixed-role pair summaries/flattening and a linear bridge; do not substitute a single RBF Gram plus MLP or ordinary attention softmax. No GP head, inducing dataset, posterior solve or marginal-likelihood objective.
cards.difference: RAT-SPN requires decomposable variable scopes and density leaves; NKN composes valid pairwise kernels with repeated overlapping input arguments and Schur products. OTKE uses a kernel inside balanced transport, whereas NKN learns the kernel algebra itself. Simple pair-dot readout lacks the entire composition network.
cards.difference_from_retained9: Unlike logic gates, conjunction/disjunction here are kernel product/nonnegative-sum closure, not relaxed truth tables. Not KAN or Lattice function composition.
cards.mask: Construct only active-token Gram blocks, or zero invalid pairs after every biased sum layer. Padding cannot alter pair denominators. Preserve role/head labels in input encodings and output grouping. Empty history bypasses.
cards.risk: Products may explode or vanish; excessive normalization can erase the intended kernel. GP extrapolation/uncertainty claims are not transferred, and positive semidefinite geometry alone does not imply task benefit. Use multiple kernel output channels to avoid a single scalar collapse.
verification_required: Primitive and composed Gram symmetry/PSD on finite sets
Gradients to primitive scales and all positive sum weights
No external support or batch axis in kernels

cards.title: Convex Potential Flows: Universal Probability Distributions with Optimal Transport and Convex Optimization
cards.source_domain: Invertible generative models and optimal transport.
cards.source_verification: Original method and raw official ICNN/DeepConvexFlow read. Author forward already returns just autograd.grad(potential.sum(), x, create_graph=True); logdet routines are separate. Plain ICNN avoids data-dependent ActNorm in ICNN2.
cards.mechanism: ICNN: z1=softplus(A1x+b1), z_(l+1)=softplus(W_l^+ z_l+A_lx+b_l), F(x)=w^+ z_L+a^T x; phi(x)=alpha||x||^2/2+beta F(x), alpha,beta>0. Output is the full gradient map T(x)=grad_x phi(x). Its Jacobian is the SPD Hessian, not an arbitrary residual MLP.
cards.transfer: Apply the complete strong-convex-potential gradient map in a compact masked fixed-role embedding and decode its representation correction. Keep the positive hidden-path weights, direct input skips and smooth convex activations. Train with unchanged task loss through mixed second derivatives. Do not compute log-density, transport objective or inverse conjugate optimization in normal forward.
cards.difference: Spline updates alternating coordinate halves with monotone scalar splines; DEQ solves a fixed-point state. CP-Flow directly differentiates a global convex scalar potential to produce a coupled vector map. Its defining condition is Hessian positivity, not a contractive residual or numerical convergence to equilibrium.
cards.difference_from_retained9: Neural ODE integrates a finite-time vector field and Sandwich constrains a Lipschitz feedforward branch. CP-Flow is an instantaneous monotone gradient map. Also distinct from proposed iResNet: positivity/strong convexity rather than spectral contraction ensures invertibility.
cards.mask: Sanitize before compact input construction. For per-head fixed-role transforms, restrict phi to the active-coordinate subspace with inactive values clamped and remask its gradient; never interpret outputs at clamped inactive coordinates as completed features. Empty history bypasses.
cards.risk: Second-order autograd costs and inference-mode incompatibility need explicit handling. Potential terms depending only on conditions have zero gradient-map effect and must not create dead trainable parameters. No claim of optimal transport to a target distribution without the source density objective; invertibility only concerns the internal continuous map.
verification_required: Autograd output matches finite-difference potential gradient
Small-dimensional Jacobian symmetry and positive eigenvalues
Task gradients to all expected ICNN parameters

additional_screened_not_counted.title: Pooling by Sliced-Wasserstein Embedding
additional_screened_not_counted.reason: Read PSWE.forward and source paper. Learned projection -> sort/interpolate -> reference displacement -> learned rank-weighted sum is too close to existing FSPool. The paper itself presents this relation; a learned reference may become a constant after linear aggregation. Not counted merely because OT terminology differs.

additional_screened_not_counted.title: Fourier Sliced-Wasserstein Embedding for Multisets and Measures
additional_screened_not_counted.reason: Original proposed-method section verified, but canonical repository currently contains README only; a related fsw-gnn implementation exists. With equal masses and fixed finite cardinalities, quantile Fourier sampling still produces rank-weighted sorted projections, close to FSPool. Not counted without stronger exact-code and non-equivalence closure.
